title: Fewest coins
statement:
A cashier has unlimited coins of each value in `coins`. Return the fewest coins that add up to exactly `amount`, or -1 if it cannot be done.

Note that taking the largest coin first does not always give the fewest coins.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What if the amount cannot be made?
Does taking the largest coin first always work?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: No, it can fail. The examples show one.
clarifyingQuestions.why: Pushes away from greedy toward dynamic programming.

clarifyingQuestions.question: How large are the amount and coin list?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Up to 12 coin values and amount up to 10,000.
clarifyingQuestions.why: A table over amounts is affordable.

edgeCases.why: Impossible even though coins are smaller than the amount.

approaches.name: Greedy, largest coin first
approaches.idea: Repeatedly take the largest coin that fits.

approaches.name: Recursion over choices
approaches.idea: Try every coin at every step.

approaches.name: Bottom-up table
approaches.idea: best[a] = 1 + min(best[a - c]) over coins c <= a, with best[0] = 0.

optimal.name: Bottom-up DP over amounts
optimal.explanation: Fill best[0..amount] with a sentinel larger than any real answer (amount + 1), set best[0] = 0, and for each a from 1 to amount, for each coin c <= a, take best[a] = min(best[a], best[a - c] + 1). Return best[amount] or -1 if it is still the sentinel.

hintLadder: Try greedy on 1, 4, 6 with amount 8. What goes wrong?
If you knew the fewest coins for every smaller amount, how would you get this one?
What is the last coin you add?
Fill a table from 0 to amount: best[a] is 1 plus the best of best[a - c] over every coin c.

expectedMentions.what: Asks what to return when the amount cannot be made
Shows or explains why greedy fails
States the recurrence on the last coin
States O(amount * k) time and O(amount) space
Explains the sentinel for impossible amounts

followUps: Count the number of ways to make the amount instead.
Each coin can be used at most once.

walkthrough.say: If it can’t be made I return minus one, and amount zero is zero coins? Unlimited coins of each value?
Greedy is tempting, but with 1, 4 and 6 for 8, greedy takes 6, 1, 1, three coins, while 4 plus 4 is two. So I need to consider every choice.

The last coin I add is some c, and the rest is the best way to make a minus c. So best of a is one plus the minimum of best of a minus c. I fill that from 0 up to the amount. That’s amount times number of coins, with O(amount) space.
amount plus one works as infinity because no answer can use more than amount coins.
For 1, 4, 6 up to 8: best of 4 is 1, best of 6 is 1, best of 7 is 2 from 6 plus 1, and best of 8 is min of best 7 plus 1, best 4 plus 1, best 2 plus 1, so 2. Correct.
For 5 and 3, nothing fits, best of 3 stays at the sentinel 4, so minus one.
O(amount times k) time, O(amount) space.
